to.title: The Fed raises by a quarter point on December 9
to.text: The FOMC raises the federal funds target range by 25 basis points, to 4.00%-4.25%, at the meeting ending December 9, 2026.

to.title: The Fed raises by a half point or more on December 9
to.text: The FOMC raises the federal funds target range by 50 basis points or more, to 4.25%-4.50% or higher, at the meeting ending December 9, 2026. Governor Waller is the only official to back it publicly; New York Fed President Williams has ruled it out.

shock.note: A half-point move against 6-7% priced would lift front-end yields by roughly 15-20bp and signal a faster path. On Nov 10, 2026, when hot CPI moved the 2-year 17bp, the S&P 500 lost 0.4% in a day; a surprise at the meeting itself, with Waller's 'shock' framing, is larger. I put the S&P 1.5% below where a quarter point leaves it.
On Nov 10 the 10-year rose 10bp for a 17bp move in the 2-year (CNN, 'Bond yields surge most in 19 months'); hawkish Fed news this month has flattened the curve, so I carry about 6bp to the long end.
A wider rate gap extends the dollar's rally; the dollar index is already at a 19-month high on hike expectations, so the further move is modest.
BND's duration is near 6 and its yields sit in the 2- to 10-year part of the curve, which moves more than the long end on a policy surprise: about 12bp there is -0.7%.

A hold, priced at about 3%, removes roughly 15bp from front-end yields. Relief for equities is tempered because a Fed that holds with core inflation running 3.5-3.7% annualised invites doubt about inflation control. I put the S&P 0.8% above the quarter-point baseline.
Lower policy-rate expectations pull long yields down while a larger inflation-risk premium pushes them up; I take the two to cancel at the long end.
The dollar's 19-month high rests on hike expectations; a hold takes some of that back.
Intermediate yields fall about 7bp on a hold; with duration near 6 that is +0.4%.

markets.question: Will the Federal Reserve Hike rates by 0bps at their December 2026 meeting?
markets.rules:
If the Federal Reserve does a Hike of 0bps on December 09, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.

The outcomes are mutually exclusive: at most one can resolve to Yes. For example, a 50-basis-point hike resolves “Hike   25 bps” to Yes and “Hike 25 bps” to No.

If the scheduled FOMC meeting is canceled and does not occur on its scheduled date, “Fed maintains rate” resolves to Yes and all other outcomes resolve to No.

markets.question: Will the Fed increase interest rates by 25 bps after the December 2026 meeting?
markets.rules:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's December 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for December 8-9, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their December meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.
